caption:
Nobody told me there was a settings page that changes everything.

ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all have a place where you can tell the AI about yourself BEFORE you ever type a single prompt.

Here's the 60-second version:

→ ChatGPT: Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions. Two boxes. One for "what should ChatGPT know about you" and one for "how should it respond."

→ Claude: Start any conversation with a system prompt, or use Projects to save your preferences permanently across chats.

→ Gemini: Tap your profile → Personal Info. Limited, but it reads your Google activity to fill in gaps.

The problem? Most people write something like "I'm a marketer who likes concise answers" and call it done.

That's like handing someone a business card and expecting them to know how you think.

The AI still doesn't know:
— Whether you want options or one clear recommendation
— If you need the "why" before the "what"
— Whether blunt feedback energizes you or shuts you down
— How much structure vs. free-form thinking you actually absorb

Custom instructions are the right idea. Most people just don't know what to put in them.

That's exactly what bootfile.ai figures out for you — your thinking style, your communication preferences, your decision-making patterns — then turns it into an instruction profile you can drop into any AI tool.

Same settings page. Completely different experience.
